target.title: Decoding spoken phonemes from sensorimotor cortex with High-Density ECoG grids
target.version: Final edited article published 2017-10-07 in NeuroImage 180(Pt A):301–311; supplied text is the PMC author manuscript.

read.pdf: Fig. 1–6 captions and Tables 1–2 read from text.txt; no separate PDF supplied

entries.text: Five epilepsy patients had subdural ECoG grids targeted at inferior sensorimotor face cortex; individual grid coverage varied with clinical surgical considerations.
entries.condition: R1 and R2 had right-hemisphere grids; L1, L2, and L3 had left-hemisphere grids; coverage was patient-specific.

entries.text: HD grids used 3–4 mm center-to-center electrode spacing; 32–128 electrodes were implanted and 32–72 analyzed per participant.
entries.quote: We refer to these grids as high density (HD) ECoG grids due to their high electrode density (3-4 mm center-to-center).

entries.text: R1, R2, L1, and L2 were recorded at 512 Hz with 128-channel Micromed; L3 was recorded at 2000 Hz with 256-channel Blackrock.
entries.condition: Micromed: R1, R2, L1, L2, 22-bit, 0.15–134.4 Hz band-pass; Blackrock: L3, 16-bit, 0.5 Hz high-pass.

entries.text: Signals were notch-filtered (49–51, 97–103 Hz), common-average-referenced within participant, converted to 65–125 Hz HFB (1 Hz increments; Gabor wavelet FWHM 4 wavelengths), log-summed, run-z-scored across electrodes, and smoothed (100 ms).
entries.unit: Hz filter bands; Hz HFB band; Hz step; wavelengths FWHM; ms smoothing kernel
entries.condition: Z-score mean and standard deviation were calculated across all electrodes in each task run, not per electrode, to preserve inter-electrode variance; fold-specific fit is not stated.

entries.text: HFB trials covered 1 s, from 500 ms before to 500 ms after VOT; rest trials were centered on their temporal midpoint.
entries.unit: s trial duration; s relative to VOT
entries.condition: VOT-aligned spoken phoneme trials; rest-trial windows centered on rest temporal midpoints.

entries.text: Native Dutch-speaking participants were visually cued to overtly produce /p/, /k/, /u/, /a:/ or remain silent; only acoustically identifiable correct productions and silent rest trials were retained.
entries.condition: Experimenter checked audio from synchronized video or Blackrock audio; acoustic variation was tolerated if the utterance remained identifiable as the cued phoneme.

entries.text: Correctly spoken phoneme and rest trial totals were R1 174/63, R2 70/16, L1 153/43, L2 119/30, and L3 114/30.
entries.unit: trials; participants R1, R2, L1, L2, L3 in that order
entries.condition: Overt task, per-participant counts after acoustic correctness screening; five phoneme classes including four phonemes and rest.

entries.text: The primary evaluation used per-participant leave-one-trial-out classification; the held-out trial was the test case, and electrode screening for STMF used the remaining trials.
entries.condition: For each fold, all but one trial were used to screen electrodes; electrodes whose mean-trial HFB differed between rest and any phoneme at p<0.05 entered the STMF feature set.
entries.quote: For classification, all trials except for one were used to screen the electrodes for inclusion in the STMFs.

entries.text: STMF class templates were concatenated mean HFB traces across electrodes over the trial; each test trial was assigned to the most-correlated template.
entries.unit: class templates; s trial window in main analysis
entries.condition: Five classes /p/, /k/, /u/, /a:/, rest; matched-filter model trained within each participant's leave-one-out fold.
entries.quote: The test trial was then classified according to the STMF it correlated highest with.

entries.text: The comparison SVM used linear kernels and one-versus-all classification under the same leave-one-out strategy; electrodes were selected for phoneme-versus-rest response.
entries.condition: Matlab 2016a fitcsvm; five-class, four-phoneme-only, and active-versus-rest datasets; per-participant leave-one-out.

entries.text: STMF and SMF were additionally evaluated in three 500 ms windows before, centered on, and after VOT; only the centered 500 ms window was reported for SMF comparison.
entries.condition: Four-phoneme-only and four-phoneme-plus-rest tasks; windows at −500–0, −250–+250, and 0–+500 ms relative to VOT.

entries.text: Empirical chance was estimated by shuffling trial labels 500 times for non-SVM analyses and 120 times for SVM, rerunning leave-one-out, and taking the upper 95% confidence bound.
entries.condition: Permutation counts differ by method due to computation time; significance threshold p<0.05; reported table chance values are per participant and task.
entries.quote: Chance levels were then determined to be the upper 95% confidence bound of the distribution.

entries.text: Reported classification accuracies were not weighted to compensate for unequal class trial counts.
entries.condition: Trial frequencies varied by class and participant; authors note this makes empirical chance differ from theoretical chance.

entries.text: Outputs were discrete class labels in three analyses: active phoneme versus rest, four phonemes without rest, and four phonemes plus rest.
entries.condition: Closed-set classification of visually cued overt productions; no word sequence or continuous speech output.

entries.text: Five-class STMF accuracy was 75.5% (SD 6.5%), mean empirical chance 26.4%; participant scores R1/R2/L1/L2/L3 were 83.1/81.4/70.4/68.5/74.1%.
entries.condition: Per-participant leave-one-out, five classes (/p/, /k/, /u/, /a:/, rest), full 1 s VOT-centered HFB trial; mean across five epilepsy participants; unweighted accuracy.

entries.text: Active-versus-rest STMF accuracy was 87.6% (SD 14.1%), mean empirical chance 27.1%; participant scores R1/R2/L1/L2/L3 were 100/81.3/100/90/66.7%.
entries.condition: Two classes: all four overt phonemes combined versus rest; per-participant leave-one-out; mean over R1, R2, L1, L2, L3.

entries.text: Four-phoneme STMF accuracy was 71.9% (SD 8.8%), mean empirical chance 29.4%; participant scores R1/R2/L1/L2/L3 were 77.0/81.4/62.1/63.0/76.1%.
entries.condition: Four overt phoneme classes (/p/, /k/, /u/, /a:/), rest excluded; per-participant leave-one-out over five epilepsy participants.
entries.quote: 4 phonemes could be distinguished at a score of 71.9% (sd 8.8%).

entries.text: Five-class SMF accuracy was 63.5% (SD 14.2%), mean empirical chance 26.4%; participant scores R1/R2/L1/L2/L3 were 83.1/68.6/64.8/45.0/55.9%.
entries.condition: Five classes (/p/, /k/, /u/, /a:/, rest); spatial matched filters omit within-trial temporal evolution; per-participant leave-one-out.

entries.text: Four-class SMF accuracy was 60.3% (SD 14.2%), mean empirical chance 27.4%; rest excluded and temporal evolution omitted.
entries.condition: Four overt phonemes only, per-participant leave-one-out; spatial matched filter; mean over R1, R2, L1, L2, L3.

entries.text: Five-class SVM accuracy was 77.2% (SD 10.2%), mean empirical chance 25.3%; participant scores R1/R2/L1/L2/L3 were 82.7/77.9/79.6/59.7/86.0%.
entries.condition: Five classes (/p/, /k/, /u/, /a:/, rest); linear one-versus-all SVM; per-participant leave-one-out.

entries.text: Four-class SVM accuracy was 72.9% (SD 12.5%), mean empirical chance 26.0%; rest excluded.
entries.condition: Four overt phoneme classes only; linear one-versus-all SVM; per-participant leave-one-out across five participants.

entries.text: The authors report no significant STMF-versus-SVM difference in the 2-, 4-, or 5-class tasks; STMF was not outperformed by SVM.
entries.condition: Comparisons across the five participants for 2-, 4-, and 5-class leave-one-out classification.
entries.quote: it was not outperformed by the SVM approach (paired t-test, p>0.3 for 2-, 4- and 5-class analyses).

entries.text: The 500 ms STMF window centered on VOT yielded 74.5% (SD 8.1%) for five classes and 72.4% (SD 8.8%) for four phonemes, comparable to full-trial results.
entries.unit: % accuracy; percentage-point SD and empirical chance
entries.condition: Five-class (/p/, /k/, /u/, /a:/, rest) and four-phoneme-only tasks; −250 to +250 ms around VOT; per-participant leave-one-out; mean over five participants.

entries.text: Five-class STMF using the 500 ms before VOT reached 64.0% (SD 8.5%), mean empirical chance 26.1%.
entries.condition: Five classes (/p/, /k/, /u/, /a:/, rest), −500 to 0 ms relative to VOT, per-participant leave-one-out over five epilepsy participants.

entries.text: The informative-electrode subsampling procedure used 5000 random subsets; the authors report the selected informative-electrode set stopped changing after 3000 iterations.
entries.condition: Randomly selected electrode subsets for STMF leave-one-out classification; subset sizes ranged from 1 to all analyzed electrodes per participant.

entries.text: Most informative electrodes clustered along the inferior central sulcus; the authors interpret their location as supporting a sensorimotor contribution to decoding.
entries.condition: Electrode contribution estimated from random subsets; fMRI task map came from 12 healthy volunteers and was used as anatomical context, not as decoder training data.

entries.text: Authors claim temporal information improves phoneme classification, consistent with rapid sequences of activity across electrodes during production.
entries.condition: STMF versus spatial-only SMF in the same five-subject, leave-one-out evaluations; five- and four-class tasks.

entries.text: Removing temporal information reduced five-class accuracy from 75.5% to 63.5% (p=0.046); four-class accuracy fell from 71.9% to 60.3% (p=0.064).
entries.condition: STMF versus SMF, mean accuracy across five participants, leave-one-out; full 1 s window; 5-class includes rest, 4-class excludes rest.
entries.quote: classification dropped considerably to 63.5% for the 5-class analysis (2-tailed paired t-test p=0.046)

entries.text: The paper presents four methodological distinctions: targeted sensorimotor face coverage, HD grids, fine-grained temporal HFB features, and a simple STMF without parameter optimization.
entries.condition: Authors compare their overt, isolated-phoneme task with prior speech-decoding studies and acknowledge cross-study task differences.

entries.text: Authors characterize STMF as requiring no parameter optimization or prior parameter selection beyond excluding electrodes that did not respond to the task.
entries.condition: This refers to the described classifier and electrode screening; it does not establish validation or generalization beyond the evaluated trials.
entries.quote: a classification technique that does not require any parameter optimization or prior selection of parameters (other than discarding electrodes that did not respond to the task)

entries.text: Authors say their results appear to exceed those of the phoneme-generation decoding studies they knew, while warning that task differences prevent direct comparison.
entries.condition: Comparison is across different datasets, tasks, vocabularies, electrode coverage, and class counts; not a matched benchmark.

entries.text: Target-paper summary of Pei et al. 2011a: approximately 41% accuracy for four vowels or consonants.
entries.condition: Four classes; generated phoneme decoding in sensorimotor cortex as grouped in the target paper's comparison; source conditions are not further detailed here.

entries.text: Target-paper summary of Jiang et al. 2016: 73% accuracy for three vowels.
entries.condition: Three classes (vowels); paper elsewhere notes that Jiang et al. reported best decoding with a 500 ms window centered on VOT.

entries.text: Target-paper summary of Mugler et al. 2015: 37% accuracy for all English phonemes.
entries.condition: 39 English phoneme classes; target paper gives no further matched condition details.

entries.text: Target-paper summary of Mugler et al. 2014: 45% accuracy for four phonemes.
entries.condition: Four classes; target paper gives no further matched condition details.

entries.text: Target-paper summary of Blakely et al. 2008: case studies reported classification around 70–75% for two classes using similar grids.
entries.condition: Two classes; similar high-spatial-resolution ECoG grids; case-study results, not a matched protocol.

entries.text: Target-paper summary of Brumberg et al. 2011: 20% accuracy for 38 classes in one quadriplegic participant; authors note 14 undecodable phonemes might bias the result.
entries.condition: One quadriplegic subject; chronic neurotrophic electrodes; 38 phoneme classes.

entries.text: Target-paper summary of Ikeda et al. 2014: approximately 43% per single electrode for imagined single-phoneme production.
entries.condition: Single imagined phonemes; results given per electrode; target paper does not specify the number of classes in this comparison sentence.

entries.text: The authors cite Herff et al. 2015 as promising evidence that continuous-speech decoding during reading aloud may be feasible; auditory cortex contributed considerably in that study.
entries.condition: Reading text aloud; continuous speech rather than isolated prompted phonemes; auditory cortex contributed.

entries.text: The authors say isolated, clearly spoken phonemes likely make decoding easier than words or syllables, so cross-study performance comparisons are uninformative.
entries.condition: This caveat qualifies the superiority comparison with prior studies using different speech tasks.

entries.text: R1 did not benefit from temporal features and had SMF performance above 80%; authors suggest optimal grid placement or trial/VOT alignment differences as possible explanations.
entries.condition: R1; spatial-only matched filter; authors speculate alignment errors or utterance-duration variation may have blurred temporal features.

entries.text: The study did not test attempted speech or communication-impaired participants, and overt speech provides somatosensory feedback absent in the intended BCI population.
entries.condition: Participants were epilepsy patients producing overt, cued isolated phonemes; no online BCI evaluation.

entries.text: Whether results from four phonemes predict performance on the full phoneme set is unknown; a limited discriminable set could imply a limited vocabulary.
entries.condition: The task used /p/, /k/, /u/, /a:/ as isolated cues; no words or full phoneme inventory were evaluated.

entries.text: The authors do not know whether phonemes can be discriminated in rapid sequences because neighboring phoneme patterns may overlap.
entries.condition: Only isolated phonemes were elicited; continuous or rapid sequences were not tested.

entries.text: The authors say electrode coverage undersampled the cortical surface, leaving about 85% of tissue between electrodes unrecorded; exhaustive topographic mapping was not possible.
entries.condition: Patient-specific, clinically constrained grids covered only part of sensorimotor face cortex.

entries.text: The number of trials was too small for a separate training and test set, so evaluation used leave-one-out classification.
entries.condition: Trial-level leave-one-out across each participant's data; no independent held-out test set.

entries.text: The authors state that BCI transfer requires further study in people who cannot communicate by speech.
entries.condition: Study cohort comprised five epilepsy patients, not the target communication-disabled population.

entries.text: Two-class SMF accuracy was 75.0% (SD 20.6%), mean empirical chance 42.7%.
entries.condition: Active versus rest (all four phonemes combined versus rest); spatial matched filter; per-participant leave-one-out; mean across R1, R2, L1, L2, L3.

entries.text: Two-class SVM accuracy was 92.8% (SD 4.6%), mean empirical chance 32.7%.
entries.condition: Active versus rest (all four phonemes combined versus rest); linear one-versus-all SVM; per-participant leave-one-out; mean across five participants.

entries.text: Four-class STMF accuracy in the 500 ms before VOT was 58.3% (SD 8.4%), mean empirical chance 28.8%.
entries.condition: Four overt phoneme classes without rest; −500 to 0 ms relative to VOT; per-participant leave-one-out; mean across five participants.

entries.text: Four-class STMF accuracy in the 500 ms centered on VOT was 72.4% (SD 8.8%), mean empirical chance 28.7%.
entries.condition: Four overt phoneme classes without rest; −250 to +250 ms relative to VOT; per-participant leave-one-out; mean across five participants.

entries.text: Four-class STMF accuracy in the 500 ms after VOT was 65.3% (SD 10.9%), mean empirical chance 29.3%.
entries.condition: Four overt phoneme classes without rest; 0 to +500 ms relative to VOT; per-participant leave-one-out; mean across five participants.

entries.text: Four-class SMF accuracy in the 500 ms centered on VOT was 55.7% (SD 16.6%), mean empirical chance 27.7%.
entries.condition: Four overt phoneme classes without rest; spatial matched filter; −250 to +250 ms relative to VOT; per-participant leave-one-out; mean across five participants.

entries.text: Five-class STMF accuracy in the 500 ms after VOT was 68.6% (SD 10.0%), mean empirical chance 26.0%.
entries.condition: Four overt phoneme classes plus rest; 0 to +500 ms relative to VOT; per-participant leave-one-out; mean across five participants.

entries.text: Five-class SMF accuracy in the 500 ms centered on VOT was 59.7% (SD 15.4%), mean empirical chance 26.3%.
entries.condition: Four overt phoneme classes plus rest; spatial matched filter; −250 to +250 ms relative to VOT; per-participant leave-one-out; mean across five participants.

entries.text: A separate anatomical comparison used previously acquired 7T fMRI from 12 healthy volunteers performing visually cued phonemes; these data supplied a group activation map, not decoder training or test trials.
entries.condition: Four phonemes; randomized sequential production at one per 15.6 s, 10 repetitions per phoneme; data from an earlier study and not published in this paper.

entries.text: Class frequencies ranged 18–22% for R2, L1, L2, and L3, and 10–25% for R1, so the five classes were not exactly balanced.
entries.condition: Five task classes; participant-specific frequencies; accuracy was unweighted despite this imbalance.

entries.text: Overt spoken responses averaged 0.8 s reaction time and 0.5 s duration.
entries.unit: s reaction time; s response duration
entries.condition: Average over the visually cued phoneme production task; five native Dutch-speaking epilepsy patients.

entries.text: The authors report that STMF-versus-SMF differences remained significant for both four- and five-class decoding using the optimal 500 ms centered window.
entries.condition: Four phonemes only and four phonemes plus rest; centered 500 ms VOT window; STMF compared with SMF.

entries.text: The authors attribute the high classification scores in part to high-density grids and the use of discrete phonemes.
entries.condition: Interpretation of the five-participant overt isolated-phoneme results; attribution is not a controlled ablation of grid density or task design.
entries.quote: The high classification scores are likely to be enabled by the use of high density grids, and by the use of discrete phonemes.

entries.text: The authors characterize phoneme-specific spatiotemporal patterns as highly reproducible, while acknowledging that the experiment uses a small, clinically constrained sample.
entries.condition: Evidence is the five-participant, within-participant leave-one-out classification of overt phonemes.

entries.text: Significant five-class decoding in the 500 ms before VOT leads the authors to suggest decoding does not depend entirely on sensory feedback; this is not a test of attempted speech.
entries.condition: Overtly produced phonemes; −500 to 0 ms relative to VOT; five classes; per-participant leave-one-out.

entries.text: The authors report that all three tested 500 ms windows yielded significant classification for the four- and five-class tasks.
entries.condition: STMF; −500–0, −250–+250, and 0–+500 ms; four phonemes only and four phonemes plus rest; leave-one-out.

entries.text: The number of task runs per participant and the number or identity of sessions are not reported, despite run-to-run variability being noted.
entries.condition: Trial-level leave-one-out is reported; no split grouped by run or session.

entries.text: Authors conclude that optimal sensorimotor phoneme decoding requires a 400–500 ms window, while warning that sluggish HFB may limit shorter-window or real-time decoding.
entries.condition: Their overt isolated-phoneme results and cited prior work; windows are centered around VOT in the cited comparisons.

entries.text: The authors propose a possible BCI use of a sliding window with roughly half-second decoding lag, but explicitly state real-time rapid attempted-speech feasibility is unknown.
entries.condition: Speculative use-time implication; not tested online and not tested with attempted speech.

entries.text: The paper gives permutation and random-subset iteration counts but does not report random-number-generator seeds.
entries.condition: Applies to 120/500 label shuffles and the 5000 random electrode-subset analysis; reproducibility seed is not specified.

entries.text: No session- or run-held-out evaluation is described; the reported split leaves out a trial, so train/test independence across sessions is unestablished.
entries.condition: Task-run count varied; no session-grouped split or cross-session test is reported.

entries.text: Evaluation is within participant; no speaker-independent or cross-participant model transfer is reported, so generalization to unseen speakers is untested.
entries.condition: Scores were computed per participant and summarized across five participants; each test fold shares the participant with its training trials.

entries.text: Run-wise HFB normalization is described, but the paper does not state whether its mean and standard deviation were fitted using only each fold's training trials or the full run before cross-validation.
entries.condition: Z-scoring was per task run across electrodes; whether the held-out trial contributed to these run statistics is not specified.
entries.quote: the log of the sum signal was z-scored for each task run

entries.text: No separate validation set, nested cross-validation, or independent model-selection set is reported; the described electrode screening is performed from the training trials in each leave-one-out fold.
entries.condition: STMF electrode selection uses all trials except the held-out trial; SVM uses the same leave-one-out strategy; STMF has no parameter tuning as stated by the authors.

entries.text: No language model, lexicon, or other use-time linguistic aid is reported; the evaluated system is closed-set phoneme/rest classification.
entries.condition: Overt isolated phoneme task; output is one of four phoneme labels or rest.

entries.text: No separate user calibration protocol or calibration-data quantity is reported; classifier fitting is described as offline leave-one-out on the elicited task trials.
entries.condition: Five epilepsy patients; visually cued overt phoneme production; per-participant offline classification.

entries.text: No online inference or measured use-time response behavior is reported; the evaluation is offline trial classification.
entries.condition: Held-out trials were classified in leave-one-out analysis; no streaming, latency, or real-time user test.

entries.text: No user confirmation step or confirmation accuracy is described for predicted phoneme labels.
entries.condition: Offline class-label evaluation only; no interactive BCI use.

entries.text: No user correction mechanism or correction outcomes are reported.
entries.condition: Offline class-label evaluation only; no interactive BCI use.

entries.text: The paper reports no deployed or implanted speech-decoding BCI evaluation; the described results are offline feasibility analyses in epilepsy patients.
entries.condition: Overt prompted phonemes, five participants, offline leave-one-out classification; attempted speech and intended users were not evaluated.

questions.q: What exactly does the headline 75.5% accuracy measure?
questions.answer: Mean five-class STMF accuracy across five epilepsy patients in within-participant trial-level leave-one-out evaluation: four overt, isolated, acoustically verified Dutch phonemes plus rest, using 1 s VOT-centered HFB trials. The mean empirical chance level was 26.4%; there was no independent held-out cohort or session test.

questions.q: Does this demonstrate decoding of attempted speech for communication?
questions.answer: No. The experiment decoded overt cued productions in epilepsy patients, not attempted or imagined speech in people unable to speak; the authors say real-time attempted-speech feasibility remains unknown.

questions.q: What benefit did temporal features provide, and did STMF beat SVM?
questions.answer: Five-class STMF reached 75.5% versus 63.5% for spatial-only SMF (p=0.046); four-class results were 71.9% versus 60.3% (p=0.064). SVM was similar and did not significantly outperform STMF (p>0.3 across 2-, 4-, and 5-class tasks).

questions.q: What evaluation conditions limit generalization and reproducibility?
questions.answer: The authors used per-participant leave-one-trial-out because trials were too few for a separate train/test set. No cross-participant or session-held-out evaluation is reported, random seeds are absent, and it is unclear whether runwise normalization statistics were fold-specific.

questions.q: What output and use-time aids were actually evaluated?
questions.answer: Only closed-set phoneme/rest class labels were evaluated offline. The paper reports no language model, calibration protocol, user confirmation, correction mechanism, or deployed online system.

questions.q: SVM electrode selection within fold? template excludes test trial? VOT method? acoustic contamination discussed? density manipulation? same-group gesture method credited?
questions.answer: Within each leave-one-out fold, not once on all trials: the SVMs used the same leave-one-out strategy as the STMFs, and electrode inclusion was based on significance against rest. The method describes screening with all trials except the held-out one. | The paper does not explicitly say whether the held-out trial was excluded when computing each class-mean STMF template. It describes the templates as means across trials and then compares them with the left-out test trial; standard leave-one-out practice would exclude the test trial, but that exclusion is not stated explicitly. | VOT was determined from the recorded audio and marked for trial alignment in Praat. The text describes marking with an annotation program and does not describe an automatic onset-detection procedure, so this is manual annotation as reported. | not discussed: the paper does not discuss acoustic or microphonic contamination, or overlap between this band and voice pitch; it defines HFB as 65–125 Hz. | No electrode-density manipulation or subsampling to larger grid spacings is reported. The 5,000 random-subset analysis instead assigned classification scores to the selected electrodes to estimate their contributions; most informative electrodes were clustered along the central sulcus, with no anterior-versus-posterior preference. On average, half of the electrodes were included in a subset. | The paper does not identify hand-gesture studies as the origin of the matched-filter method. Its same-group hand-gesture references include Bleichner et al. (2016), “Give me a sign: decoding four complex hand gestures based on high-density ECoG,” and Branco et al. (2016), “Decoding hand gestures from primary somatosensory cortex using high-density ECoG.” In the text, Branco et al. is cited as an example of aligning trials by HFB-response timing (“decoding gestures”), not as the method's origin; Bleichner et al. is cited in discussion of motor/sign-language cortex.
